payload.title: The split arm holds a group whenever any two of its seats judged different trees, but the consumer refuses a mixed tree only for an anchor-grade closing set with no dissenter, so the stated reason for the hold (the producer follows the law that will refuse its arbiter's answer) does not hold for a split group, which always has a dissenter.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:1377-1380 (closing is built from the rows that agree with the settled verdict)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:1521-1525 (the consumer refuses a mixed tree only when len(closing) >= ANCHOR_MIN_JUDGE_COUNT and dissenting == 0)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:715-727 (_group_tree asks tree_is_mixed of ALL non-arbiter seats; the docstring says it cannot drift from the law that will refuse the answer)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:808-813 (arbitration_groups sets split and hold from the same seats)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1002-1009 (the split arm holds and mints nothing)
aria-kernel/tests/test_arbiter_minted_at_the_pairs_tree.py:365-369 (a test pins the split hold, so the broader predicate is green by construction)
payload.rule_violated: One mixed-tree law (feedback_store.tree_is_mixed): the producer is meant to be asked the consumer's own refusal condition, not a wider set of rows than the consumer inspects.
payload.notes: Group {seat 1 true_positive at A, seat 2 false_positive at C}: when the weighted vote is active (non-empty judge weights) an arbiter answering true_positive leaves closing = 2 agreeing rows and dissenting = 1, so the consumer's tree check is skipped and the group settles at sub-anchor grade with no target_sha. The split arm instead holds it, so it stays unsettled with no repair, and the held share the lead reads at M5 and M6 counts split groups the consumer would have settled. Under the legacy unanimity path the consumer never settles a 2-1 split either, so the hold changes nothing there. Close condition: Derive the split arm's hold from the consumer's refusal condition (an anchor-grade closing set) instead of from every seat, or record in a test and the registry that mixed-tree split groups are held on purpose with their repair item; the test settles a TP-at-A / FP-at-C split through the arbiter and asserts no target_sha_mixed refusal. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
